caller_census.contract: void - the result is the mutation of *this. The register the body leaves behind holds the second std::string data pointer (loaded at 0x61bd5f2), not a value, and no caller reads it.

call_sites.argument: lea rdi, [rdi + 0x60] - the object is a member of the caller's own receiver (a sub-object at +0x60)

caller_census.method: raw byte scan of .text for the `e8 rel32` direct-call encoding whose target is the routine entry, each hit confirmed by decoding exactly 5 bytes; forward/backward context decoded in <=0x180-byte windows; FDE attribution from .eh_frame; rax taint walk with the caller-saved set killed at every intervening call.
caller_census.reachability_note: Every site reaches its (empty) use on the fall-through path inside the owning FDE within a handful of instructions, so no site's answer is path-dependent. The two callers that stack two consecutive Reset calls (0x5dfd1e0 and 0x5dfd544) each pass a distinct object ([rsp + 0x68] of different frames).

observations: The routine is a leaf: no call, no indirect branch, no branch of any kind, no relocation, and no stack frame - its whole effect is 18 stores to memory that either the object or the object's own pointers name.

It is an inlined aggregate zeroing: `pxor`/`xor` produce the zeros once, then twelve 16-byte `movups` plus three 8-byte and one 2-byte store cover the object, skipping +0x4a..+0x4f and the 16-byte string metadata blocks at +0xc0 and +0xe0.

Two of the eighteen stores are argument-dependent: the body loads a `std::string` data pointer out of the object at +0xc0 / +0xe0 and writes a single NUL through it. That is an inlined `std::string::clear()` - the size word at +0xc8 / +0xe8 is zeroed, the pointer and capacity are preserved, and the buffer keeps its allocation.

Because those two writes follow the object's own contents, the write set is not expressible as a fixed address list: it is a fixed object offset list plus two pointer dereferences. The packet proves both halves - the closed-form model and the decoded-bytes emulator agree row for row on all 300 ledger rows, and the field rows are identical in every one of them.
The routine is idempotent (all eighteen writes store zero), which the packet tests explicitly.

A self-referential (SSO) string is handled the same way: the object's pointer names an address inside the object, the NUL lands there, and the write count is unchanged at 18 - no size-dependent branch exists.

The object offset +0x48 is written with a two-byte store while every neighbouring field is 16 or 8 bytes wide, so bytes +0x4a..+0x4f survive a Reset. This is the sort of detail a reconstruction-from-prose would get wrong.

All eight callers discard the register the body leaves in rax (the census taint walk drops it within a few instructions or at the next call), confirming the void contract; none of them reads it as a value.
unknowns: Which rocksdb field each offset names in 0.11.0+8.1.1 is not recovered: the offsets are fixed by the binary, the field names are not. The two `std::string` members at +0xc0/+0xe0 are inferred from the load-then-one-byte-zero shape and from the 16-byte gap that follows each, which is what libstdc++'s SSO layout produces.

The eight caller FDEs carry no symbols in the stripped image, so they are identified by address range only; no claim is made about which method each one is. The member-object call at 0x5dfe710 is the only one whose `rdi` is derived from the caller's own receiver.
The three identical source copies the vendor census records (identical_source_count = 3) are not enumerated individually; the reconstruction is bound to the sha256 of the body.
claim_anchors: semantics.tsv: 24 anchors, one per instruction, contiguous over the whole 127-byte window (sizes sum to 127); verify.py re-decodes each anchor's bytes with Capstone (exactly one instruction, same length, same mnemonic family) and matches its text against the committed excerpt
ledger: cases.tsv: 300 stratified rows (all-zero, all-0xFF, alternating, five object lengths, three buffer fill values, self-referential vs arena strings, random patterns) with the model and the decoded-bytes answer for each; 0 disagreements
sweep: verify.py: 150 further cases over {5 object lengths} x {5 fill bytes} x {2 string shapes} x {3 buffer bytes}, plus an idempotence check and three doctored-excerpt checks that prove the emulator executes the committed bytes rather than echoing the model
